{{Short description|Measure of how far an individual test result deviates from the median}}
{{cs1 config|name-list-style=vanc}}
A '''multiple of the median''' ('''MoM''') is a measure of how far an individual test result [[Deviation (statistics)|deviates]] from the [[median]].  MoM is commonly used to report the results of [[Screening (medicine)|medical screening]] tests, particularly where the results of the individual tests are highly [[Statistical dispersion|variable]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Wald|first=Nicholas|date=1976|chapter=The detection of neural tube defects by screening maternal blood.|title=Prenatal Diagnosis|volume=Les Colloques d'inserm|issue=61|pages=227–38|publisher=I.n.s.e.r.m. |isbn=978-2855981482}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Wald|first=Nicholas|date=1977|title=Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein measurement in antenatal screening for anencephaly and spina bifida in early pregnancy|journal=Lancet|volume=309|issue=1|pages=1323–1332|doi=10.1016/s0140-6736(77)92549-1 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=All MoMs are not equal: some statistical properties associated with reporting results in the form of multiples of median| pmid=7679245 | volume=52|issue=2|pmc=1682205|journal=Am J Hum Genet|pages=425–30|vauthors=Bishop JC, Dunstan FD, Nix BJ, Reynolds TM, Swift A | year=1993 }}</ref>

MoM was originally used as a method to normalize data from participating laboratories of [[Alpha-fetoprotein]] (AFP) so that individual test results could be compared. 35 years later, it is the established standard for reporting maternal serum screening results.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aphl.org/conferences/proceedings/Documents/2013/2013-Newborn-Screening-Symposium/23Berberich.pdf|title=Using Multiples of the Median (MoM) for Normalization of TREC Results Meets the Need for Standardized SCID Reporting|last=Berberich|first=Stanton L.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203010905/https://www.aphl.org/conferences/proceedings/Documents/2013/2013-Newborn-Screening-Symposium/23Berberich.pdf|archive-date=2013-12-03}}</ref>

An MoM for a test result for a patient can be determined by the following:
:<math>MoM(Patient) = \frac{Result(Patient)}{Median(PatientPopulation)}</math>

As an example, [[Alpha-fetoprotein]] (AFP) testing is used to screen for a [[neural tube defect]] (NTD) during the second trimester of pregnancy. If the median AFP result at 16 weeks of [[gestation]] is 30&nbsp;ng/mL and a pregnant woman's AFP result at that same [[gestational age]] is 60&nbsp;ng/mL, then her MoM is equal to 60/30 = 2.0. In other words, her AFP result is 2 times higher than median.
